about.title: About | Eolietech
about.description: Eolietech is a set of private file tools made by candygoogy, a developer from the Aeolian Islands. Why it runs in your browser, and why the code is open source.
about.lede: A set of file tools that work without uploading your files, made by one developer from the Aeolian Islands.
about.origin.p1: Eolietech is made by candygoogy (that's the handle), a developer from the Isole Eolie, the volcanic Aeolian Islands off the north coast of Sicily. The name comes from there: Eolie, plus tech.
about.origin.p2: The islands are where the project comes from, not what it sells. The site itself is black, white and grey, so your files and the tools stay in front. Two colours come from the islands: the deep teal of the Tyrrhenian Sea, used for links and buttons, and the orange of Stromboli's lava at night, kept for the logo.
about.palette.label: The palette
about.privacy.p1: Most online file tools upload your file to a server, process it there and send the result back. That asks for a lot of trust when the file is a scanned ID, a signed contract or a voice memo, and you can't see what happens to it on the other side.
about.privacy.p2: Browsers can now do this work themselves. Compressing an image, merging PDFs or even running a speech model is fast enough on an ordinary laptop or phone. So Eolietech does the work there, and your file never has to travel.
about.open.p1: A privacy promise you can't check is only a promise. The code is licensed under AGPL-3.0, so anyone can read what each tool does, run it themselves or point out a problem.
about.open.p2: The AGPL also means that anyone who runs a modified copy as a public service has to publish their changes under the same licence.
about.money.p1: The free tools cost very little to run, because your device does the work. A paid plan, Pro, will come later for features that need servers, such as large AI models and an API. There are no ads.
about.cta.security: How to check the privacy claims
security.title: Security: check that your files stay private | Eolietech
security.description: How to confirm that Eolietech never uploads your files: the Content-Security-Policy header, the Network panel test, the offline test and the open source code.
security.lede: Eolietech says your files never leave your device. This page shows how to confirm that with nothing but your browser.
security.how.p1: When you choose a file, the tool reads it inside the page and processes it with code running on your device, often compiled to WebAssembly. The result is created in your browser and saved straight to your downloads. The file is never sent to a server.
security.csp.p1: Every page on eolietech.com is sent with a Content-Security-Policy header: a set of rules your browser enforces on the page, whatever the page's own code tries to do. For your files, the rule that matters is this one:
security.csp.p2: It means scripts on the page can only open network connections (fetch, XHR, WebSockets, beacons) to eolietech.com itself. If any code tried to send data to another server, the browser would block the request and log an error in the console.
security.csp.caveat: To be precise: 'self' still allows connections to eolietech.com. The only server endpoint on the site is the Pro waitlist sign-up, which accepts an email address. The network test below shows that the tools don't call it, or anything else, with your files.
security.csp.view: To see the header, open your browser's developer tools (F12, or Cmd+Option+I on a Mac), select the Network tab, reload the page, select the first request and find content-security-policy under Response Headers. From a terminal:
security.csp.full: The full policy, as served today:
security.csp.rule.script: script-src: code can only come from eolietech.com, plus Cloudflare Turnstile for the waitlist spam check. 'wasm-unsafe-eval' lets the tools run WebAssembly.
security.csp.rule.worker: worker-src: the background workers that do the heavy lifting must come from eolietech.com.
security.csp.rule.media: img-src and media-src: images and audio can only come from the site itself, or from data: and blob: URLs, which hold your own files in memory.
security.csp.rule.frame: frame-src: the Turnstile check is the only thing that can be embedded.
security.csp.rule.form: form-action: forms can only submit to eolietech.com.
security.network.s1: Open a tool page, then open developer tools (F12, or Cmd+Option+I on a Mac).
security.network.s2: Select the Network tab and clear the list.
security.network.s4: Look at the requests. The first time you use a tool you may see its code, WebAssembly modules or an AI model being downloaded from eolietech.com. Those are downloads to you. Nothing is uploaded, and nothing goes to any other domain.
security.network.tip: Select a request and open its Payload tab to see what it sent. Code downloads send nothing.
security.offline.s1: Open a tool and process one file, so everything the tool needs has loaded.
security.offline.s2: Disconnect: turn on airplane mode, or choose Offline in the Network tab's throttling menu.
security.offline.s3: Process another file. It still works, because none of the work needs a server.
security.code.p1: Eolietech is open source under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0. The source repository holds the code of every tool and the headers file quoted above.
security.never.1: Upload the files you open in a tool.
security.never.2: Show ads or load advertising scripts.
security.never.3: Sell or share data about you.
security.never.4: Ask for an account to use the free tools.
security.others.p1: The site is hosted on Cloudflare. Like any web host, Cloudflare handles standard request data when you load a page, such as your IP address and the page address. It never receives your files.
security.others.p2: The Pro waitlist on the pricing page uses Cloudflare Turnstile to keep out spam sign-ups. It loads on that page only.
